# Read Data Through Key Vault And cdiofabric

This example reads the ODBC connection string from Key Vault.

The connection string uses the `cdiofabric` managed identity to connect to Fabric.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = FALSE)
```

# 1. Connect

```{r connect}
if (!requireNamespace("AzureKeyVault", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("AzureKeyVault")
if (!requireNamespace("DBI", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("DBI")
if (!requireNamespace("odbc", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("odbc")

vault <- AzureKeyVault::key_vault("https://uzima-fabric-tokens.vault.azure.net/")
connection_string <- vault$secrets$get("fabric-odbc-connection-string")$value

# To use another database, change only the database name.
# connection_string <- sub("DATABASE=uzima_db_backup;", "DATABASE=Fitbit;", connection_string)

con <- DBI::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), .connection_string = connection_string)
```

# 2. See Available Tables

```{r list-tables}
tables <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME
  FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES
  ORDER BY TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME
")

head(tables, 30)
```

# 3. Read A Small Sample

Change `table_to_read` to the approved table or masked view you need.

```{r read-sample}
table_to_read <- "dbo.dimenrolledparticipants"

sample_data <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, paste("SELECT TOP 10 * FROM", table_to_read))
sample_data
```

# 4. Close The Connection

```{r disconnect}
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```
